who: Historian of modern Europe at Cornell since 2013; PhD EHESS, 1989.

evidence.says: Cornell identifies Traverso as a historian of modern and contemporary Europe, with an EHESS PhD in 1989 and a Cornell appointment beginning in 2013.
In this March 2019 interview, Benedetta Carnaghi names Enzo Traverso as her advisor at Cornell and describes her comparative dissertation on Fascist and Nazi spies.
The candidate item names Enzo Traverso, lists Cornell as an employer and EHESS as an educational institution, and carries LC identifier n92092348.

notes: Direct student testimony, appointment period and doctorate match.

who: Roman historian at the University of Arizona since 1992; PhD Berkeley in Ancient History and Mediterranean Archaeology, 1991.

evidence.says: Her CV records the Berkeley PhD in December 1991 and Arizona employment from August 1992. Page 9 lists her as doctoral dissertation committee chair for Matthew Coleman (2013–2016) and Adam Donaldson (2009–2012).
LC identifies Alison Futrell, author of Blood in the Arena, and cites her Arizona faculty page describing her research on imperial Rome, spectacle and gender.

notes: Both listed students and their completion years are corroborated by her CV; the doctorate matches the AHA school.

who: Historian of European and American intellectual and political history at Brandeis; PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: Brandeis identifies Mark Hulliung as Richard Koret Professor Emeritus of the History of Ideas in History, with a Harvard PhD and research in European and American intellectual, cultural and political history.
The 2013–2014 History bulletin lists Mark Hulliung on the faculty in European and American intellectual, cultural and political history.
LC identifies Mark Hulliung, with variant Mark L. Hulliung, and cites the Brandeis faculty guide naming him Richard Koret Professor of the History of Ideas.

notes: The authority record explicitly identifies the Brandeis professor; institution, period, field and Harvard doctorate agree.

who: Professor of Classics and Ancient History at Cincinnati from 1970; specialist in Hellenistic settlements, PhD Princeton, 1970.

evidence.says: The departmental memorial states that Getzel Cohen joined Cincinnati in 1970, became associate professor in 1976 and full professor in 1982, and specialized in Greek history and Hellenistic settlements, the subject of his 1970 Princeton dissertation.
The publisher identifies Getzel M. Cohen, author of The Hellenistic Settlements in Europe, the Islands, and Asia Minor, as Professor of Classics at Cincinnati.
LC identifies Cohen, Getzel M., citing The Seleucid Colonies and Breaking Ground, and also records the name Getzel Cohen.

notes: The shorter advisor name corresponds to Getzel M. Cohen, whose ancient-history appointment covers both student years.

who: Historian of Canadian military and political history at McGill; PhD University of London.

evidence.says: McGill's 1999–2000 calendar lists Carman Miller among History professors, with a University of London PhD.
McGill lists Carman Irwin Miller in History and Classical Studies with emeritus status beginning June 1, 2010.
LC's Carman Miller record identifies a King's College, University of London PhD and the chairman and associate professor of McGill's History Department.
McGill Archives describes Carman Miller's research as Canadian military and political history and records his joining McGill History in 1967.

notes: The candidate authority identifies the same McGill historian; faculty service precedes and emeritus status follows the 2007–2008 student years.

who: Andy Albert den Otter, historian at Memorial University, faculty 1972–2007 and subsequently professor emeritus.

evidence.says: Memorial's fall 2009 convocation program, page 12, names Sean Cadigan and Andy den Otter as Norma Jean Hall's supervisors for her History dissertation on Hudson Bay seafarers, 1508–1920.

LC identifies A. A. den Otter as Andy Albert den Otter, records the variant Andy Albert den Otter, and cites a publisher biography describing Memorial History service from 1972 to 2007 and subsequent emeritus status.

notes: The full-name authority and direct supervision record resolve Andy to the candidate. Hall's thesis title is worded differently in the convocation program but has the same subject and date range.

who: Historian of medicine at Queen's, Hannah Chair 1988–2017; PhD in History and Philosophy of Science, Sorbonne.

evidence.says: Queen's identifies Duffin with Philosophy and History, a Sorbonne PhD in History and Philosophy of Science, and tenure of the Hannah Chair in History of Medicine from 1988 to 2017.
The 2012 History newsletter identifies Jacalyn Duffin as one of Casey Hurrell's PhD supervisors and describes Hurrell's research on the World Health Organization and postwar medical humanitarianism.
LC identifies Jacalyn Duffin, author of Langstaff and To See with a Better Eye, as the Hannah Chair in History of Medicine at Queen's University.

notes: Candidate authority, appointment period, medical-history field and direct supervision of Hurrell agree.

who: Historian of Germany and co-operatives at Saskatchewan; PhD Oxford in Modern History.

evidence.says: Saskatchewan identifies Fairbairn as a historian and professor emeritus with an Oxford PhD in Modern History, and records his service as university provost in 2008–2014.
The fall 2012 convocation list names Brett Fairbairn as supervisor of Mark Andrew McCulloch's History PhD, Consumption Junction, What's Its Function?

LC identifies Brett Fairbairn, with variants Brett T. and Brett Thomas Fairbairn, as a professor in Saskatchewan's Johnson-Shoyama Graduate School of Public Policy and a fellow at its Centre for the Study of Co-operatives.

notes: The Oxford doctorate, Saskatchewan appointment and direct McCulloch supervision record confirm the match.
